corrections.source_says: The exclusion field should record the reported participant flow: 1,047 people initially entered; 36 failed the attention check, 67 contributed fewer than five discussion messages and had average message length below 20 characters, 20 did not complete the post-task survey, and 19 completed an individual task that did not match their assigned discussion task. The final primary-analysis sample was 905 people. Separately, 34 people with mismatched display-name identifiers were excluded only from BDI analyses, leaving 871 for those analyses. The initial-entry count is not explicitly a randomized count, so n_randomized should remain null.

confirmed: The local source is arXiv:2512.18234v1, dated 20 December 2025, labelled Preprint submitted to Elsevier; the title and author list match the form (PDF p. 1). The actual PDF has 64 pages, with Appendices A-H on pp. 26-64, despite the printed footer saying of 65. The entire markdown, including all appendices, was read.

S1 is an online randomized people experiment: Prolific participants worked in triads randomly assigned to human-only teams or teams containing supportive, contrarian, or mixed-persona generative-AI teammates, across creative, analytical and ethical tasks. online_rct and context_class none are supported, and the study belongs in the two-screener pipeline (PDF p. 2, Introduction; pp. 3-6, Sections 3.1-3.2 and Figure 2).
The final main sample is 905 people clustered within 572 groups, not 905 texts or ratings; a pre-exclusion randomized total is not explicitly given (PDF pp. 3-4, Section 3.1; p. 52, Table 28).

All arm counts match Table 2. In Survival Ranking / Ethical Dilemma / Creative Writing order: H3 95/93/90; H2_C 60/61/62; H2_S 60/61/57; H1_C 29/29/30; H1_S 29/30/29; H1_M 30/30/30. The creative-writing H3 cell alone exceeds the people threshold (PDF p. 6, Table 2).

The creative task requires a movie plot with AGI central to the story, including characters, setting, events and resolution (PDF p. 28, Appendix A.3). The procedure is individual baseline, a 10-minute group discussion, then individual post-task work, supporting after_ai for the recorded performance gain (PDF p. 5, Section 3.2; p. 6, Figure 2).

Two trained researchers, blinded to condition, scored creative output on originality, elaboration and coherence; final ratings averaged the raters. Performance gain is post-task minus baseline, and continuous outcomes were standardized before analysis (PDF pp. 9-11, Sections 3.7 and 3.9; p. 33, Table 9).

The reported string and one-line finding match Table 28: Creative H2_S versus H3, CR2 Est. = 0.336, SE = 0.184, df_Satt = 61, p_Satt = .074, p_Holm = 1.00. Creative and H3 are the reference categories; the contrast shows no statistically clear improvement. CR2 inference clusters by group (PDF p. 52, Table 28 and note; p. 13, Section 3.11).

S2 is a separate pilot with 15 people, each interacting with two AI teammates, yielding 30 humanness ratings on a 7-point scale. It has fewer than 50 people, reports no randomized comparison or creativity score on participant output, and is explicitly excluded from the main experiment (PDF p. 8, Section 3.5).

The supplement description is supported: coded exemplars are mentioned on p. 10, Section 3.7; Appendix G names external spreadsheets on pp. 56-58, including SI_z_gain_EMMs_BDI_minus.xlsx, SI_z_gain_EMMs_BDI_plus.xlsx and SI_z_gain_CR2_BDI_CR2.xlsx on p. 58. These files are not embedded in the PDF and were not read.

The experimental model/provider and preregistration are not stated in the document; persona prompts are included (PDF pp. 7-8, Sections 3.4-3.5; pp. 29-31, Appendix B; full-document check). This is an empirical experiment with a separate pilot, not a synthesis, so synthesis defaults are appropriate (PDF pp. 3-13, Methods).
summary: The online randomized study belongs in the two-screener pipeline and scores participants' creative output. Recorded counts and the Table 28 statistic match the PDF, but exclusions and the stated primary-outcome status need correction.
